# Repository Custom Instructions — z1engine

## What this repository is

z1engine is a C++17 game engine for Windows x64 only. Rendering is OpenGL via GLAD + GLFW with an ImGui editor UI and a render graph supporting deferred and forward pipelines. ECS is EnTT. Scripting is Python 3.14 via pybind11. Builds use Premake5 generating VS2026 projects (`z1engine.sln` at repo root); outputs go to `engine/bin/<Config>/` (editor/game/tests), intermediates to `engine/intermediate/`.

## Commands (always use the dev CLI — never invoke tools directly)

Run everything through `python dev/z1.py <command>`:

- `generate` — regenerate VS projects after adding/removing source files (required before building)
- `compile [--config Debug|Release|Profile]` — build the solution
- `format [--dry-run]` — enforce tabs/whitespace/CRLF
- `validate-shaders` — validate all GLSL shaders
- `test [--filter <pattern>]` — run `test_*.exe` suites
- `smoke --frames <N>` — launch editor, render N frames, exit cleanly
- `benchmark --suite <name>` — performance regression check
- `dcv --auto` — full develop-compile-verify loop for complete changes
- `gen-pybinds` — regenerate Python bindings from reflected types
- `release` — package release folder

Never invoke `devenv.com`, MSBuild, `shader_validator.exe`, or test executables directly; never wrap commands in `cmd //c`. Judge pass/fail from the `RESULT:` JSON line the dev scripts print, never from exit codes alone. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 build error, 2 validation error, 3 runtime error, 4 configuration error.

Minimum verification before declaring done: `compile` passes with 0 errors. Run tests/shaders/smoke as applicable; complete changes require `dcv --auto` to pass end-to-end.

## Project layout

- `engine/runtime/` — core engine runtime
- `engine/editor/` — ImGui editor
- `engine/game/` — game code
- `engine/bakery/` — asset processing (namespace `z1::bakery`)
- `engine/test/` — unit tests (`test_<name>.cpp`, auto-discovered by `create_test()` in `premake5.lua`)
- `engine/3rdparty/` — third-party code; never edit without explicit authorization
- `premake5.lua` — build definitions; new `.cpp`/`.h` files must be covered by its globs
- `dev/z1.py` — dev CLI entry point
- `openspec/kb/` — agent-consumable project knowledge base (architecture, build, coding-style, testing, dev-scripts, etc.); read relevant pages, never re-derive their content
- `openspec/specs/` and `openspec/changes/` — spec-driven change artifacts (see workflow below)

## Coding style (mandatory)

- Comments: line comments ≤ 1 line; module/class comments ≤ 3 lines; multi-line comments only for whole-system or concept explanations
- Hard tabs (width 4), K&R braces, CRLF line endings, `#pragma once` headers
- `PascalCase` types, `camelCase` functions, `m_` member prefix, east-const (`Type const&`), namespace `z1`
- Ownership via `std::shared_ptr`/`std::unique_ptr`; raw pointers non-owning only
- Include order in `.cpp`: `pch.h` first, then own header, same-module, other-module, 3rdparty, stdlib; blank line between groups
- Logging via `CORE_DEBUG`/`CORE_WARN`/`CORE_ERROR`/`CLIENT_INFO`; `PROFILE_FUNCTION()` on hot paths
- Prohibited: `using namespace std;`, `std::endl`, `std::cout`/`std::cerr` for diagnostics, raw owning `new`/`delete`, `#ifndef` guards
- Match the local style of the file being edited if it differs slightly

## Change workflow

Features and behavior changes follow the OpenSpec lifecycle: `proposal.md` → `design.md` → `specs/<capability>/spec.md` → `tasks.md`, implemented in order with validation gates between task groups. Use the skills in `.github/skills/` (openspec-propose, openspec-apply-change, openspec-archive-change, openspec-explore). On completion with passing verification, archive the change under `openspec/changes/archive/`.

After adding/removing source files, run `generate` before compiling. Update `openspec/kb/` (and its `index.md`) when the work surfaced new, non-trivial project knowledge.

## Commit conventions

Conventional Commits: `<type>: <description>` (`feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`). AI-generated commits are prefixed `[AI]` and carry trailers `Generated-by: Copilot` and `Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>`. Fully AI-generated files carry a `[AI-GENERATED]` header comment.
